title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving emergency Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) to ensure immediate access to food to the most vulnerable households in Xudur District of Bakol Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe MARDO Drought Response project will provide lifesaving emergency humanitarian assistance to address the urgent crisis caused by severe and prolonged drought conditions in Hudur, Bakol Region. The project's core intervention consists of unconditional cash transfers (UCT) of $55 per household per month for three consecutive months, totaling $132,000 in direct cash assistance. This transfer value represents approximately 70% of the minimum food expenditure basket, calculated based on local market assessments conducted by the Food Security Cluster for Southwest State. The cash enables families to purchase essential food items, including staple foods, pulses, vegetables, and animal products from local markets, preventing further deterioration in nutritional status while simultaneously supporting local market economies. ltbrgtltbgtWHERE: Geographic Focus and Contextlt/bgtltbrgtThe project targets eight severely drought-affected rural villages in Xudur District, Bakol Region, Southwest State, Somalia: Gomorey, Weeroe, Tuboy, Shidle (Shiidle), Daryeel, Gaabaney, Cusbo Eelo, and Banjinaya. These remote pastoral and agropastoral communities have experienced devastating livestock losses, depleted household assets, and collapsed traditional livelihoods due to consecutive failed rainy seasons. Current assessments reveal alarming humanitarian indicators: approximately 60% of households are experiencing moderate to severe food insecurity (IPC Phase 3-4), 18% of children under five years of age suffer from acute malnutrition, and access to safe drinking water has become increasingly scarce as water points dry up. ltbrgtltbgtWHEN: Project Timeline and Strategic Timinglt/bgtltbrgtImplementation will occur from January 20 to July 19, 2026, during the critical lean season when food stocks are low, market prices peak, and income opportunities dwindle. Cash distribution will occur in months 2, 3, and 4, after a month for community sensitization, beneficiary registration, committee formation, and accountability setup. The timing is crucial, as it provides support before the next anticipated agricultural cycle and prevents households from resorting to harmful negative coping strategies such as selling remaining productive assets, marrying off children, migrating to dangerous locations, or reducing meal frequency and dietary diversity. ltbrgtltbgtWHO: Target Beneficiaries and Vulnerability Criterialt/bgtltbrgtThe project directly helps 800 of the most at-risk households, including 500 headed by women and 300 headed by men. It is expected to reach a total of 4,800 people (about six people per household). The beneficiary selection employs rigorous vulnerability-based targeting criteria developed in consultation with community leaders and humanitarian standards. Priority populations include female-headed households that are more economically vulnerable and socially isolated households with children who are severely malnourished and need immediate nutritional support elderly-headed households without able-bodied income earners households with disabled people who have extra trouble getting help and finding work.ltbrgtltbgtHOW: Implementation Methodology and Approachlt/bgtltbrgtMARDO will implement the project using a comprehensive and accountable methodology, ensuring assistance reaches the most vulnerable while maintaining program integrity and beneficiary safety. The process begins with district-level coordination meetings with Area-Based Coordination (ABC) and Food Security Cluster chairs to ensure no duplication, followed by community sensitization sessions where project objectives, targeting criteria, entitlements, duration, and complaints mechanisms are clearly communicated. Beneficiary identification employs vulnerability-based targeting (VBT) through inclusive community committees (10-12 members per village, representing women, youth, individuals with disabilities, and minority clans) who identify the most drought-affected households using transparent selection criteria. ltbrgtlt/pgt
